memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "These are the regulations for any defiling skin disease, for a sore, for defiling molds in fabric or in a house, and for a swelling, a rash or a shiny spot, to determine when something is clean or unclean. These are the regulations for defiling skin diseases and defiling molds." - Lev 14:54-57 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The long section that began in chapter 13 closes with a summary. And the purpose is stated in one phrase: to determine when something is clean or unclean.

Step back and look at what these two chapters have shown us. Corruption is real and it spreads. God examines patiently and thoroughly. Nothing is hidden from Him. And He is committed to restoration — going outside the camp, providing for the poor, cleansing homes, releasing birds into open sky.

But feel the weight too. Every cleansing here was temporary. The disease could return. The mould could reappear. The priest would have to come again, and blood would have to be shed again. This system diagnosed and managed, but it could never finally end the problem.

That is why these chapters ache with anticipation. Israel needed something these regulations could not give.

Then Christ came. He touched the untouchable and made them clean. He suffered outside the gate. He offered one sacrifice for all time and sat down. And He has promised a day when no one will ever say "I am ill" again, when God wipes every tear and makes everything new (Rev 21:4-5).

Read Leviticus 14 and you will understand why the gospel is such good news.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How have these chapters deepened your understanding of sin?
2. What does it mean to you that Christ's cleansing never needs repeating?
3. What do you most look forward to about the new creation?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that You are the cleansing these chapters could only picture. Thank You for making me clean once for all, and for the day when nothing will ever be unclean again. Amen.
